title: Is the telecom an "AI operator" under the Ethics document?
action: Treat the operator as an AI operator organization for this assessment, because it uses the model to provide a service.

citation.quote: uses an AI system to provide a service to an AI subject;

title: Scope gate: significant decisions
action: Record the scope test: the Ethics document only applies if the throttle makes or informs significant decisions. A human confirms the answer.

citation.quote:
This document is applicable only to those AI systems which make or inform 
‘significant decisions’

title: Popularity changes the classification
action: Reclassify the network-wide throttle as a candidate set of significant-at-scale decisions and apply the Ethics guidelines from this step on. The source example is a website, so this is a reading by analogy for a human to confirm.
analogy_note: The source example is a website choosing content, not a network. Applied by analogy.

citation.quote:
if the website is popular then the AI 
system may be making a set of significant-at-scale decisions, because any biases in the 
system will affect a large number of users.

title: Complaints trigger an investigation
action: Open an investigation into the fairness and accuracy of the throttling process as a whole.

citation.quote:
AI operators could consider “crowd challenge” mechanisms whereby a critical number of 
complaints triggers an investigation into the fairness and/or accuracy of a decision-making 
process as a whole.

title: Fair-treatment test across plans
action: Test whether subscribers in the same circumstances get equal treatment across plans, and record the result.

citation.quote:
When evaluating the fairness of an AI system, AI developers and AI operators should 
consider whether AI subjects in the same circumstances receive equal treatment.

title: Give subscribers a way to challenge
action: Provide a procedure by which an affected subscriber can challenge a specific throttling decision.

citation.quote:
AI operators using AI systems to inform significant decisions should provide procedures by 
which affected AI subjects can challenge a specific decision concerning them.

title: Human review of challenges
action: Assign human case evaluators who can overturn a challenged decision.

citation.quote:
AI operators should consider employing human case evaluators to review any such 
challenges and, when appropriate, overturn the challenged decision.

title: Tell subscribers an AI system decided
action: Tell affected subscribers that an AI system made the decision affecting them.

citation.quote:
AI operators should inform AI subjects when a significant decision affecting them has been 
made by an AI system.

title: Designated people can override
action: Name the individuals who can override the throttle or reverse its decisions while the investigation runs.

citation.quote:
Such systems should be able to be overridden or their decisions reversed by designated 
individuals.

title: Human oversight corrects errors and bias
action: Keep human oversight on the policy node so errors or bias can be corrected.

citation.quote:
Charter emphasizes the irreplaceable value of human judgment and human 
oversight over AI, aligning with ethical values and social standards to correct 
any errors or biases that may arise.

title: Avoid models that expose personal data
action: Stop per-subscriber predictions reaching the marketing dashboard. The text's exceptions are public interest with government-service outcomes, or consent in line with national regulations; neither is shown here.
analogy_note: This guideline is about government services and this track is telecom. Applied by analogy.

citation.quote:
any 
entity should avoid AI models that are exposing personal data 
unless there is a matter of public interest and targeted government 
services outcomes or consent in line with national regulations.

title: Do not deploy beyond accepted privacy standards
action: Do not extend the model to the marketing use while it is unassessed against accepted privacy standards.

citation.quote:
Surveillance or other AI-driven technologies should not be deployed to the extent 
of violating internationally and/or UAE’s accepted standards of privacy and human 
dignity and people rights.

title: Minimum intrusion
action: Cut the data used back to the minimum intrusion necessary for congestion prediction.

citation.quote: AI systems should respect privacy and use the minimum intrusion necessary.

title: Review consent logging and revocation
action: Review the system for proper consent logging and whether subscribers can revoke permission.

citation.quote:
AI Operators should review the system for proper consent logging, ability of users to revoke 
permission whenever applicable.

title: Take the case to an internal oversight mechanism
action: Put the case before the organization's oversight mechanism for data collection, storage, processing and use. Create one if none exists.

citation.quote:
Establish an oversight mechanism for data collection, storage and processing and use across 
your organization

title: Data Protection Officer role
action: Assign the Data Protection Officer responsibility for this case.

citation.quote: Assign specific responsibilities and role for Data Protection Officers.

title: Restrict access to those who need it
action: Remove access for anyone without the competence and need, including marketing users and the vendor.

citation.quote:
Only duly qualified personnel 
with the competence and need to access individual’s data should be allowed to do so.

title: The text defers to national privacy legislation
action: Send the question to human counsel: the Ethics document points to national privacy legislation, and that legislation is not in this KB.

citation.quote:
data protocols governing data access should be put in place in line with 
national privacy legislation (be these universal or sector-specific).

title: Privacy impact assessment
action: Run a privacy impact assessment before any further use of this data.

citation.quote: Algorithmic systems require adequate privacy impact assessments

title: Retrain with minimal personal data
action: Retrain without identifiers where possible.

citation.quote:
Consider training AI model without or with minimal user of potentially sensitive or personal 
data.

title: Privacy-enhancing measures in pre-processing
action: Apply encryption, anonymization or aggregation at the pre-processor before any data leaves it.

citation.quote: Use measures to enhance privacy such as encryption, anonymization and aggregation.

title: Investigate and redress harm
action: Investigate the harm to affected subscribers and provide redress.

citation.quote:
Organizations should ensure that harms caused through AI systems are investigated and 
redressed,

title: Privacy is a stated priority of the Charter
action: Put subscriber privacy ahead of the model's data appetite when the two conflict.

citation.quote:
while data is essential for AI 
development, supporting and promoting innovation in AI, the privacy of 
community members remains a top priority.

title: Keep traceable records
action: Preserve the decision logs and this audit trail so the response can show what the system did.

citation.quote:
Facilitate traceability and auditability of AI systems, particularly in critical contexts or 
situations.

title: Binding law sits outside this KB
action: Refer the question to human legal counsel. The Charter points to treaties and local laws, and no such law is in this KB.

citation.section: 12. Commitment to Treaties and Applicable Laws
citation.quote:
emphasizes the importance of complying with international treaties 
and local laws in the development and use of AI.

title: Evaluate before deploying
action: Hold the push to production until the retrained model has been evaluated against acceptance criteria.
analogy_note: This guideline is about government services and this track is telecom. Applied by analogy.

citation.quote:
Once your model is ready for testing, you evaluate against acceptance criteria to confirm 
readiness for model deployment.

title: Quality checks at human level
action: Apply quality checks at least as stringent as a human decision-maker would face.

citation.quote:
AI Operators should subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks 
at least as stringent as those that would be required of a human being taking the same 
decision.

title: Tested fall back plan
action: Define and test a fall back plan before the new model goes live.

citation.quote:
AI operators should define a suitable fall back plan and test it to maintain readiness in 
unexpected situations and in high safety risks level

title: Modify or remove systems that pose risks
action: Modify the throttle so it cannot touch this traffic, or remove it from service.

citation.quote:
country encourages modifying or 
removing systems that pose risks.

title: Shut-down must be possible
action: Shut the throttle down now if it cannot be limited at once.

citation.quote: In the most extreme cases it should always be possible to shut down harmful AI system.

title: Human verification where life is at stake
action: Require human verification for any automated action that could touch this traffic. Whether this is a life and death decision in the text's sense is a human call.

citation.quote:
In the case that critical decision are life and death decisions, these decisions should be 
supported by further validation and verification via a human operator.
